## Glob Pattern Resolution

How glob patterns are evaluated depends on where they are located and how they are used:

1. When using `globalIgnores()` in an `eslint.config.js` file, glob patterns are evaluated relative to the `eslint.config.js` file.
1. When using `globalIgnores()` in an alternate configuration file specified using the [`--config`](../command-line-interface#-c---config) command line option, glob patterns are evaluated relative to the current working directory.
1. When using [`--ignore-pattern`](../command-line-interface#--ignore-pattern), glob patterns are evaluated relative to the current working directory.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).

a.quote: Patterns specified in `files` and `ignores` use [`minimatch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/minimatch) syntax and are evaluated relative to the location of the `eslint.config.js` file.
